title: Binary Tree Level Order Traversal
statement: You get the root of a binary tree. Return its values grouped by level: first the root alone, then its children left to right, then the next row, and so on, as a list of lists. An empty tree gives an empty list.

example.caption: Row by row from the top: [3], then [9, 20], then [15, 7].

idea.sentence: Use a queue, and before each round freeze its size: exactly that many nodes are the current level, and their children line up behind them.

jargon.plain: A line where you add at the back and take from the front: first in, first out.
Visit everything one step away, then everything two steps away, and so on, level by level.

watch.inputHint: One argument: the tree as a level-order array, null for a missing child, e.g. [3,9,20,null,null,15,7]

compare.bruteLabel: For each depth d, search the whole tree for nodes at depth d
compare.optimalLabel: One queue pass over all nodes
compare.unit: node visits, for a skinny tree

rows.name: Re-scan for each depth
rows.note: Walks the whole tree once per level. Slow on a tall tree.

rows.name: Queue (BFS)
rows.note: Each node enters and leaves the queue once. The queue holds at most one widest level plus its children.

fast.takeaway: A queue makes the tree come out in rows by itself. Freezing its size at the start of a round tells you where one row ends and the next begins.

stages.title: Queue the root
stages.note: An empty tree returns an empty result. Otherwise the queue starts with just the root.

stages.title: Freeze the level size
stages.note: At the start of a round, everything in the queue is one level. Remember how many nodes that is.

stages.title: Take a node, queue its kids
stages.note: Remove the front node, record its value, and add its children to the back. They belong to the next level.

stages.title: Level complete
stages.note: After exactly that many nodes, add the finished row to the result. The queue now holds the next level.

edges.title: Empty tree
edges.why: Return an empty list of levels, not a list holding one empty level.

edges.title: Single node
edges.why: One round, one node, and no children to queue.

edges.title: Left chain
edges.why: Every level has exactly one node. The queue never holds more than one.

edges.title: Gaps in the middle
edges.why: Missing children are skipped, so 4 and 5 sit side by side in the same level.

gotchas.text: Read the queue size before the inner loop, not inside its condition. The queue grows while you loop, so a live length would swallow the next level.
Push children only if they exist. Pushing null makes the next round crash when it reads node.val.
queue.shift() is O(n) in theory, but V8 handles small arrays well. For huge trees keep a head index instead of shifting.
shift() is typed as returning TreeNode | undefined. The non-null ! is safe here because the loop only runs while the queue has items.
queue = queue[1:] drops the front without copying. Return a non-nil empty [][]int for an empty tree so JSON shows [], not null.
Make a fresh level slice each round. If you reuse one slice and append to it, earlier rows in result change too.

recap.key: Queue the root. Each round, take exactly queue-length nodes (one level), record them, and queue their children.
recap.complexity: Time O(n). Space O(w) for the widest level.
moves: size = queue length, make an empty level
Pop size nodes: record each, push its children
Add the level to the result and repeat
